scope: Existing ordinary data codec paths for prepared-child Date/Map/Set/RegExp, per-encoding graph identity and local handle cleanup. No new callable ownership, native Wasm routing, WeakMap/WeakSet copying, live mirroring or persistent data-cache policy.

baseline.outcome: Both browsers rejected methods on all four foreign data kinds with missing-slot errors. The separate own-realm Date→Map-key/Set-value graph also lost shared identity in baseline source.

implementation: Memoize only immutable internal-slot membership through captured harmless native Date/Map/Set/RegExp operations. Read current values and flags with captured native operations; iterate stored entries via captured native forEach.
Reuse existing data-copy branches before public-prototype plain-record classification. Known intrinsic ctor/proto mapping remains earlier.
One encoding owns duplicated memo handles until all sibling references are encoded. Argument encoding shares one scoped graph; Date/RegExp decoding reuses its existing local seen table.

Original container, property, entry/key, earlier argument and receiver handles are released on failed child encoding. Existing persistent plain-record/array caches are not rolled back or otherwise redesigned.
controls: Native methods accept the actual child-realm instances before guest projection.
Foreign and own Date keys/Set membership, repeated Map/Set/RegExp references, self/cross cycles and decoded graph identity are preserved.
Changing public prototypes to null and overriding size/iterator/forEach/getTime/source/flags does not determine data kind or extraction.
Date value changes and NaN are read fresh; a public Map tag does not grant Map slots.
Controlled map entry-copy, array-copy, record-copy and argument-copy failures preserve the error and dispose cleanly; registered native callee remains uncalled.
Restoring module instanceof predicates reproduces foreign slot failures while the own graph remains fixed.
limits: Browser fixtures use synthetic local data and native prepared-child constructors; no code-generation invocation or outside connections. Full application/performance and complete confinement qualification remain with the integrating branch.
